page: Microsoft Azure F4alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Faldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a high base clock speed of 4.5 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI. The server is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It includes a bundled 472 GB local NVMe SSD and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the F4alds_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core CPU testing and Geekbench single-core scores. Single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also achieve top-tier results. Multi-core and memory performance metrics generally fall within the average range, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 8843.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 69.97 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is measured at 839.11 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 53.52 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. For lightweight machine learning workloads, the server achieves a top-tier text generation speed of 343.49 tokens/sec using a small 135M LLM, but performance drops to the bottom 25% for medium 7B model prompt processing.

The F4alds_v7 offers a specialized hardware profile that trades memory capacity for high-frequency compute power. With only 2.0 GB of RAM per core, it is not designed for memory-intensive applications or large-scale database hosting. However, the inclusion of a high-speed 472 GB local NVMe SSD provides strong local storage performance, making it highly cost-efficient for workloads that require fast temporary storage alongside high-frequency single-core processing. This server is best suited for single-threaded processing tasks, software compilation, lightweight web serving, and small-scale text or image processing pipelines where high CPU clock speeds are prioritized over large memory footprints.
